name: Anomalous prime-field group
domain: E/F_p, p prime
recognition: Verify a nonsingular model and #E(F_p)=p, equivalently trace t=1.
witness: Exact point count, field and model coefficients, and selected point order.
construction: Search nonsingular short Weierstrass models and count points; keep only trace-one models.

name: Smooth selected subgroup
domain: Any finite cyclic elliptic subgroup
recognition: Factor the actual selected generator order and bound its largest prime-power component.
witness: Generator, exact order, complete factorization, and membership of the target.
construction: Count a candidate curve, factor the group order, then certify a point with smooth exact order.

name: MOV / Weil-pairing transfer
domain: Selected r-subgroup of E/F_q, gcd(r,q)=1
recognition: Compute k=ord_r(q), so r divides q^k−1; small k is a screening signal.
witness: Independent r-torsion pairing argument, explicit nondegenerate image of the chosen generator, and target transport.
construction: Choose q,r,k with r | #E(F_q) and ord_r(q)=k; construct E and certify pairing data.

name: Frey–Rück / Tate-pairing transfer
domain: Selected r-torsion, gcd(r,q)=1
recognition: Check the multiplicative embedding degree k=ord_r(q) for the chosen r.
witness: A Tate-pairing class giving an injective image of the chosen subgroup, plus destination-field DLP cost.
construction: Start with r | #E(F_q), compute k, and exhibit the Tate-pairing auxiliary input.

name: Supersingular pairing geometry
domain: Supersingular E/F_q with selected r
recognition: Certify supersingularity, selected r and its embedding degree; compare target-field arithmetic.
witness: Point-count and supersingularity certificates, r-subgroup generator, pairing transfer, and destination cost.
construction: Choose a supersingular family, count the curve, and certify a prime-to-characteristic r-subgroup.

name: Binary-field GHS descent
domain: E/F_(2^N) with a specified nontrivial subfield tower, N composite
recognition: A composite binary-field tower selects a possible descent; compute the exact coefficient magic number and Type I/II condition, including the relative trace of b, before applying the genus formula. Price a destination solver only with its declared factor-base and smoothness assumptions.
witness: Field tower and coefficient basis, magic-number and Type I/II certificates, relative trace, correct genus, explicit cover and subgroup map, actual usable factor base, ordinary-query relation yield and rank, target descent, and qualified complete destination cost.
construction: Screen extension-field coefficients by the published GHS descent conditions, then construct and check the cover.

name: Odd-characteristic GHS covering
domain: Prime extension degree d∈{2,3,5,7}, odd characteristic
recognition: Match a published case and realize its equations and covering conditions for the exact model.
witness: Defining equations, smoothness/genus, cover map, Jacobian isogeny, selected subgroup injection, and cost.
construction: Choose one of 36 published cases, instantiate parameters over the finite field, and certify each geometric gate.

name: Cubic norm-one genus-three branch
recognition: Require a norm-one λ and exact model witness; v₂(f_π)≥2 is a necessary class screen, not a decision rule.
witness: λ=α^q/α, exact coefficients, cover and genus certificate, subgroup map and charged construction.
construction: Choose λ in ker Norm_(F_(q³)/F_q), solve α^q=λα, and build y²=x(x−α)(x−α^q).

name: Nonsplit quadratic genus-three branch
recognition: Use the exact second-branch class oracle and model witness; keep it separate from cubic support.
witness: Exact model, covering construction, genus and induced subgroup map.
construction: Select a class admitted by the nonsplit quadratic-torus branch, then construct and verify its representative.

name: Direct extension-field decomposition
domain: Selected subgroup of E/F_(q^d), d>1, with an explicit subfield factor base
recognition: Fix the extension representation, subgroup, actual usable factor base, decomposition system, and query law; bound fixed-base relation support before interpreting a filtered acceptance rate.
witness: Exact base digest and usable count, accepted-query law, support bound, all attempts including rejects, verified natural relations, rank growth, final linear algebra, target descent, scalar replay, and a matched one-target reference.
construction: Use a subfield factor base and solve the summation-polynomial decomposition system on the original elliptic curve.

name: Cover-and-decomposition index calculus
method: Intermediate-field cover followed by Jacobian decomposition
domain: Selected subgroup G of E/F_(p^(nd)) over a composite-degree tower F_(p^(nd))/F_(p^n)/F_p; sextic branches n=2,d=3 or n=3,d=2
recognition: Construct H/F_(p^n) and a cover H→E over F_(p^(nd)); certify that norm after pullback is injective on G. A same-field cover alone does not establish this route.
witness: Exact tower, lower-field H and map, selected-subgroup kernel, actual usable F_p-abscissa base, accepted-query support bound, verified natural relations and useful rank, final linear algebra, target descent, and complete cost.
construction: For F_(p^6), test the H/F_(p²) genus-three and H/F_(p³) genus-two branches separately; use the bihomogeneous quadratic sieve only for the odd-characteristic n=2 hyperelliptic branch.

name: Index-calculus relation support and rank
domain: A selected subgroup with a frozen factor base, summand policy, and target-query law
recognition: For B actual usable classes and unordered positive m-sums with repetition, support has at most binomial(B+m-1,m) targets. Under a uniform accepted set of size A, hit probability is at most min(1,support/A); a filter may change A but cannot enlarge fixed support. Measure useful rank separately.
witness: Curve/subgroup and base identities, actual usable B, exact summand and sign policy, certified or bounded accepted-set size A, rejected and accepted attempts, independently verified relations, novel rank per query, matrix and target costs, and a matched one-target reference.
construction: Freeze the curve and base, prove the support cap for the exact combination policy, construct known-scalar ordinary queries, and measure accepted-query relation yield and useful rank. Enlarge the usable base or change the relation mechanism when capacity is insufficient.

name: Reduced-divisor support geometry for index calculus
method: Fixed-origin divisor splitting and support-overlap screen
domain: A selected subgroup transported to a genus-g Jacobian with a frozen fixed-origin divisor base and target-query law
recognition: Reduce each usable class to a divisor relative to one origin, factor its residual support polynomial over the lower field, and compute pairwise support gcds. Check whether each degree-g divisor is special: for a smooth plane quartic at degree three, three distinct noncollinear support points give h0(D)=1 and a unique effective representative at that origin. Recompute actual factor-base size, accepted rank-bearing target support, known-scalar anchor overlap, and projected relation rank after any splitting filter. A splitting type or shared point is a collector input; the danger decision follows verified rank and complete cost.
witness: Exact cover and subgroup map, fixed-origin divisor certificates, squarefree support polynomials, independent factorization and gcd replay, noncollinearity or Riemann-Roch certificate where uniqueness is asserted, selected usable class identities, frozen query law, known-scalar equations, target-support and rank census, and complete one-target costs.
construction: Stratify reduced classes by rational support orbit type and specialness, screen shared residual support, select a factor-base policy, then replay ordinary known-scalar queries and eliminate fresh support-point columns before measuring rank and cost. If h0(D)=1 at the chosen origin, seek another class, origin, or higher-degree relation to vary its support.
source: P-192 Type I divisor-support and split-base certificate (2026)

name: Plane-quartic line-section relation graph
method: Residual-line splitting, subgroup projection, and private-column rank
domain: A smooth genus-three plane quartic with an explicit subgroup projection, a finite rational point base, and a frozen line/query policy
recognition: Enumerate pair-lines through the selected rational point base, factor each degree-two residual intersection, and project every new point into the DLP subgroup. Distinguish nonspecial source divisors from reduced cofactor-projected subgroup classes. For an elliptic quotient class Q, take its unique r-torsion half H, both inverse-fiber signs, and the full three-step Frobenius orbit; the six-point fiber divisor can descend whether the third Frobenius step fixes or swaps the signs. Census all four cubic-field character cells: the ++ predicate is a query-law filter, not a necessary cubic-reduction condition. Check fixed-origin cubic cuts and quotient images independently. Count projected point reuse, signed collisions, pair-sum collisions, and useful relation rank after fresh columns are included. A danger verdict requires relation yield, target descent, and complete cost.
witness: Exact quartic and subgroup map, frozen point list and pair order, residual quadratic equations and splitting certificates, inverse plane-to-cover maps, subgroup and sign checks, all-character fiber census, prime-field cubic input pairs, fixed-origin degree-three divisors, independent PARI cubic-cut and three-quotient-image replay, formal line rows, known-scalar query law, useful rank, and one-target costs.
construction: Generate rational residuals from selected pair-lines, project their point classes, build the incidence graph with one column per distinct subgroup point, seek cycles or function-divisor identities that eliminate private columns, then test ordinary known-scalar queries and complete target recovery.
source: P-192 Type I line-support and all-character quotient-reduction certificates (2026)

name: Three-sum support capacity and scalar-query overlap
method: Exact multiset-image bound, subgroup support census, and query-law denominator
domain: A prime-order elliptic subgroup with generator G, an actual distinct usable base of B subgroup classes, and a frozen known-scalar three-sum query law
recognition: Enumerate or certify the distinct nonidentity three-sum support M and collision-row rank. The universal cap is M <= binomial(B+2,3). For ideal uniform nonzero scalar a with target -2[a]G in an odd prime-order subgroup, one-query overlap probability is exactly M/(r-1), and q-query success is at most qM/(r-1). A geometry-conditioned law requires the support count and ambient subgroup population in each selected cell; a larger eligible support share alone is not a measured hit-rate gain. Keep base construction, relation rank, target descent, and complete one-target cost separate.
witness: Exact curve and subgroup generator, base-point digest and usable count, complete pair/triple support count and sorted-point digest or a sound exhaustive certificate, identity exclusion, independently replayed point additions and r-torsion checks, collision-row rank, frozen scalar stream, per-cell support and population when conditioned, and verified relation and target-cost receipts.
construction: Build a usable subgroup base, enumerate distinct three-sum targets and additive collisions, apply the uniform multiset capacity bound, then sample or certify the chosen geometry-cell denominator and relation yield under a frozen known-scalar law. Promote a danger finding only after useful rank, descent, and complete matched cost are verified.
source: P-192 Type I exact three-sum support and Lean capacity theorem (2026)

name: Known-scalar anchor overlap for index-calculus relations
method: Exact support collision and relation-row test
domain: A selected subgroup with a frozen signed factor base, summand policy, known-scalar anchor set, and target-query law
recognition: Separate three-sum targets with nonzero unknown-log rows from targets with independently known scalars, including zero-row sums. A chosen known-scalar anchor supplies an unknown-log equation only at a target overlap; repeated rank-bearing targets supply a new equation only when their formal signed-point vectors differ. Count both intersections and the rank of resulting row differences modulo the subgroup order.
witness: Exact curve and subgroup, signed base-point identities, known-scalar certificates, complete target-key and formal-vector census, independent collision replay, geometry acceptance law, useful row rank, and measured query and recovery costs.
construction: Enumerate frozen sums, coalesce by exact group target, compare full formal vectors, include zero-row anchors, test target overlap, then sample independently known-scalar queries and measure accepted novel rows and rank. A positive overlap is a relation candidate, not a complete attack cost.

name: Adaptive factor-base rank balance
method: Eliminate fresh logarithm columns before counting useful relations
domain: A selected subgroup and relation collector that adds new factor-base points while constructing known-scalar equations
recognition: Count every newly introduced unknown logarithm column. If each new row has its own private new point with unit coefficient, every old-log assignment extends uniquely and the rows constrain no old logarithm. Measure rank after eliminating new columns; require a second independent representation, a known logarithm, or a collision cycle to obtain positive projected rank.
witness: Exact old and new point identities, independently known query scalars, subgroup and geometry checks for new points, duplicate and old-support collision census, augmented matrix columns and rank, projected rank on the old columns, and complete query and elimination costs.
construction: For each proposed adaptive query, record its new point and row, replay the group equation independently, eliminate new columns, and count only surviving equations in the old unknowns. Test geometric eligibility and ordinary-query yield separately from algebraic rank.

name: Cubic Weil-restriction Jacobian isogeny
method: Direct isogeny to a genus-three Jacobian
domain: Selected prime-order subgroup of E/F_(q^3) satisfying the isogeny construction
recognition: Test the stated (ell,ell,ell)-isogeny conditions for the exact Weil restriction and construct the destination genus-three curve.
witness: Explicit isogeny and genus-three Jacobian, selected-subgroup kernel check, transported points, destination solver, and full cost.
construction: Follow Tian's cubic-extension construction; its homomorphism does not require a covering map C→E.

name: Selected points over a proper subfield
method: Descent to a smaller point group
domain: E/F_(p^n) with a proper subfield
recognition: Show the selected points, not only the j-invariant or a model, descend to the smaller field.
witness: Explicit field isomorphism/model transport and point-containment certificate for generator and target.
construction: Lift a curve from a proper subfield, select points in that subfield, and verify exact orders.

name: Isogeny transfer to an assessed neighbor
method: Explicit same-field isogeny and selected-subgroup transport
domain: E/F_q with a recorded separable isogeny and selected subgroup order r
recognition: Find a certified map to a curve with a separately assessed criterion; same point count identifies an isogeny class but does not supply a map or advantage.
witness: Exact endpoint models and UIDs, degree, kernel, forward map, image order of the selected generator, target transport, and construction cost.
construction: Enumerate rational kernels for chosen degrees, compute and verify Vélu codomains, then replay generator and target transport along an ordered route.

name: GLV endomorphism screen
domain: Prime-field curves with a computable endomorphism; the j=0 and j=1728 automorphisms are simple sufficient screens
recognition: For j=0 require a nontrivial cube root of unity in F_p; for j=1728 require a square root of -1. Certify the endomorphism's action on the selected r-subgroup.
witness: Explicit endomorphism, eigenvalue modulo r, orbit size, scalar-decomposition or rho implementation, and matched cost.
construction: Choose a compatible CM curve and subgroup, construct its rational endomorphism, and certify its subgroup eigenvalue.

name: GLS Frobenius-twist screen
domain: Curves over F_(p²) built as a quadratic twist of an F_p curve
recognition: Verify the twist descent and the induced Frobenius endomorphism on the exact F_(p²) model; extension degree two alone is insufficient.
witness: Twist isomorphism over its defining extension, endomorphism formula, selected-subgroup eigenvalue, and measured orbit or decomposition gain.
construction: Construct a GLS twist from a prime-field curve, retain its field representation and maps, and check the subgroup action.

name: Pairing-assisted decisional Diffie–Hellman
method: DDH decision through a nondegenerate pairing
domain: A specified cyclic subgroup and DDH input law, often with a distortion map or cross-group input
recognition: Check whether the protocol's DDH challenge can be mapped into both inputs of an efficiently computable nondegenerate pairing.
witness: Exact challenge group, pairing, auxiliary map or G2 input, nondegeneracy on the chosen subgroup, and the decision equation.
construction: Select a supersingular subgroup with a certified distortion map or define a cross-group pairing challenge; keep CDH and DLP as separate goals.

name: Static Diffie–Hellman with oracle access
domain: A fixed secret key reused across chosen public inputs in a specified protocol
recognition: Record the oracle query interface, key reuse, response form, target subgroup, and available auxiliary structure.
witness: Concrete oracle transcript model, query bound, reduction or recovery algorithm, and independently checked secret or shared-key result.
construction: Instantiate a protocol and fixed-key oracle on a named subgroup, then test a published static-DH algorithm under that oracle budget.

name: Minimal pairing output field
domain: r coprime to p, base field q=p^m and k=ord_r(q)
recognition: Compute d=ord_r(p) independently of k=ord_r(p^m); the smallest field containing the r-th roots of unity is F_(p^d), with d dividing mk.
witness: Exact p, m, r, modular-order certificates for d and k, pairing computation field, and image field.
construction: Choose p,m,r with r dividing #E(F_(p^m)); compute d and k, then compare output-field and pairing-computation costs.

name: Pairing groups G1, G2 and GT
domain: Pairing-friendly curve with a specified r, twist, and target field
recognition: Record G1 on E(Fp), G2 on the twist over F_(p²), and GT inside F_(p^k)* as three distinct order-r groups.
witness: Exact base and twist equations, generators, order/cofactor facts, embedding degree, and nondegenerate pairing specification.
construction: Import a named pairing-friendly standard with exact variant parameters; verify each group's source-defined role.

name: Pairing subgroup and cofactor validation
method: G1/G2 membership and GT result validation
domain: A concrete protocol accepting G1/G2 points or GT values
recognition: Check point-on-curve and [r]P=O for each accepted G1/G2 input when required; check GT order and final exponentiation for accepted target values.
witness: Exact input parser, cofactor policy, membership tests, adversarial inputs, and observed protocol response.
construction: Test the actual implementation with valid subgroup, off-subgroup, infinity, and malformed inputs under its published acceptance rules.
source: CFRG Pairing-Friendly Curves draft, subgroup membership

name: GT finite-field discrete-log cost
domain: Order-r target group GT in F_(p^d)*
recognition: Assess the multiplicative subgroup in the minimal output field and the particular finite-field DLP algorithms applicable to its representation.
witness: Exact p, r, d, field tower, factorization assumptions, calibrated algorithm and resource estimate.
construction: Specify a pairing-friendly parameter set and benchmark the best applicable destination-field DLP model independently of G1 and G2.
source: CFRG Pairing-Friendly Curves draft, security estimates

name: SIDH/SIKE auxiliary-torsion key recovery
domain: SIDH-style protocol public keys containing images of auxiliary torsion points
recognition: Match the public-key torsion images, starting-curve endomorphisms, and isogeny degree structure required by Castryck–Decru.
witness: Exact protocol parameter set, public-key format and auxiliary images, attack implementation, and key-recovery transcript.
construction: Instantiate SIKEp434 from its source parameters and reproduce the published key-recovery experiment.
